method: Least-squares camera resection from manually picked image points of OSM footprint vertices. Ground points (z = 0) constrain position/heading/FOV; points high on the same vertical building edges contribute only their horizontal residual with height left free, so they constrain pitch/roll without using any building height.
pickedBy: Sunvision maintainers, by inspecting web/public/examples/nyc-ridge-street/photo.jpg (2000x2000); estimated picking accuracy ±15 px

groundPoints.what: left end of the left (Ridge Street) facade at the sidewalk
building corner (centre of the chamfer) at the sidewalk
right end of the right (Rivington Street) facade at the sidewalk

verticalPoints.what: same left edge, under the parapet
same right edge, under the parapet

note: Vertex indices refer to the target footprint ring in scene.base.json; vertex 1 projects left of the optical axis, vertex 3 right (checked by bearing from the geotag).
hfovRangeSource: EXIF 29 mm-equivalent focal length on a square crop: 41.9° (centred crop, no rescale) to 61.6° (full frame width).
status: Superseded for the shipped example: the vertex-1 picks are inconsistent (they mark the end of the ornate bays, not the end of the 28 m OSM edge; 433 px off under the regularity-aligned camera). web/public/examples/nyc-ridge-street/scene.base.json now ships the auto-aligned camera (provenance inferred) and keeps this resection as history in camera.notes. See docs/research/alignment.md §4.4 (b).
